1.why: All seven screens are static single-column cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs anywhere.

2.why: Each step has one large bold dark-blue heading and a single filled teal primary button, so the key action stands out, though the dark Logs panel competes visually for attention.

3.why: Each screen holds only one field and one button, but the user must hunt for the token/code inside a technical Logs panel below the card, which slows finding what she needs.

4.why: Password rules and code length are shown on screen, but she must still carry a long random token and a six-digit code from the Logs panel into the input fields.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing familiar is presented back to her — no masked email/phone hint (the page deliberately gives the same response), and the token is an unrecognisable random string.

7.why: Sentences are short, but wording is jargon-heavy ('non-identifying contact value', 'recovery token', 'MFA', 'mock delivery', 'Prepare recovery instructions').

8.why: No error message is visible in any of the seven screenshots; only a highlighted field border appears, with no text describing a problem or how to fix it.

9.why: Fields have no placeholder examples or sample values; only the password rule text and 'six-digit' description hint at the required format.

10.why: The single path (password reset then six-digit code) is clearly labelled, but no alternative sign-in choices such as face or biometric login are offered or explained.

11.why: Every step presents just one task with one or two inputs and a single button, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Dedicated confirmation screens ('Sign-in confirmed', 'Privacy conditions accepted') plus timestamped log entries state the outcome of each action.

13.why: Each card carries a one-line instruction and a persistent security tip, but there are no contextual help links, tooltips, or progress guidance for new steps.

14.why: No back, cancel, 'resend code', or 'request a new token' controls are visible, so recovering from a mistyped entry or expired token is not supported on screen.

15.why: All seven steps reuse the identical header, card, button styling, security notice, Logs panel, and footer, making the layout highly predictable.
